```{r Import the Data}
all_species <- readRDS('Data/all_species.rds') #for tree
vertebral_counts <- read.csv('Data/vertebral_counts_master.csv')
```

```{r Data Wrangling}
#group according to species (and other variables) and calculate the standard deviation of the RAW precaudal, caudal and total counts
vertebral_counts_intraspecific_variation <- vertebral_counts %>% 
  group_by(
    species_name) %>%
  summarise(
    ln_length_ln_width_sd = sd(ln_length_ln_width, na.rm=TRUE),
    ln_length_ln_width = mean(ln_length_ln_width, na.rm=TRUE),
    precaudal_count_sd = sd(precaudal_count, na.rm = TRUE),
    precaudal_count = mean(precaudal_count, na.rm = TRUE),
    caudal_count_sd = sd(caudal_count, na.rm = TRUE),
    caudal_count = mean(caudal_count, na.rm = TRUE),
    total_count_median = median(total_count, na.rm = TRUE),
    total_count_iqr = IQR(total_count, na.rm = TRUE),
    total_count_sd = sd(total_count, na.rm = TRUE),
    total_count = mean(total_count, na.rm = TRUE),
    total_count_cv = total_count_sd / total_count, #coefficient of variation, may not be necessary mean range of vertebrae is narrow between species (25-40)
    n_count = n()
  )

vertebral_counts_intraspecific_variation_filtered <- 
  vertebral_counts_intraspecific_variation %>%
  filter(n_count >= 5.00)
```

```{r Import Tree}
#import the tree
mcgee_2020 <- read.tree('Phylogenies/phylogenies_mcgee_2020/phylogeny_mcgee_2020.tre')

#format tip labels to match the formatting of the species_names in data-frames
mcgee_2020$tip.label <- gsub("_", " ", mcgee_2020$tip.label)

#ladderise the tree
mcgee_2020 <- ladderize(mcgee_2020)
```

```{r Fitting Individual Species BAR ~ TC Linear Models}

#fit linear models for each species with at least 10 individuals, note that for some of them the vertebral counts are the same between individuals and will therefore be undefined.
within_species_linear_models <- vertebral_counts %>%
  group_by(species_name) %>%
  filter(n() >= 10) %>%
  group_split() %>%
  map_df(~ {
    mod <- tryCatch(
      lm(ln_length_ln_width ~ log(total_count), data = .x),
      error = function(e) NULL
    )
    
    if (is.null(mod)) {
      return(tibble(
        species_name = unique(.x$species_name),
        slope = NA_real_,
        slope_se = NA_real_,
        p_value = NA_real_,
        r_squared = NA_real_,
        n = nrow(.x)
      ))
    }
    
    coefs <- summary(mod)$coefficients
    if (nrow(coefs) < 2) {
      return(tibble(
        species_name = unique(.x$species_name),
        slope = NA_real_,
        slope_se = NA_real_,     
        p_value = NA_real_,
        r_squared = NA_real_,
        n = nrow(.x)
      ))
    }

    tibble( 
      species_name = unique(.x$species_name),
      slope = coefs[2, 1],
      slope_se = coefs[2, 2],   
      p_value = coefs[2, 4],
      r_squared = summary(mod)$r.squared,
      n = nrow(.x)
    )
  })

#remove NA values (i.e. species where no intraspecific variation is present)
within_species_linear_models <- na.omit(within_species_linear_models)

#prune the mcgee 2020 tree to data
within_species_linear_models_pruned_tree <- drop.tip(mcgee_2020, 
                                            which(!mcgee_2020$tip.label %in% within_species_linear_models$species_name))

#subset data frame to include only species present in the pruned tree
#subset according to the phylogeny
within_species_linear_models_subsetted <- within_species_linear_models[
 within_species_linear_models$species_name %in% within_species_linear_models_pruned_tree$tip.label, 
]
#convert to dataframe
within_species_linear_models_subsetted <- as.data.frame(within_species_linear_models_subsetted)
#set rownames as species_names for ease later
rownames(within_species_linear_models_subsetted) <- within_species_linear_models_subsetted$species_name

#reorder data frame based on the order of tip labels in the pruned tree
within_species_linear_models_subsetted <- within_species_linear_models_subsetted[
  match(within_species_linear_models_pruned_tree$tip.label, within_species_linear_models_subsetted$species_name), 
]
```

```{r Do Small Sample Sizes Increase Slope Noise?}
ggplot(within_species_linear_models_subsetted, aes(x=n, y=slope))+
  geom_point()+
  geom_smooth(method = "lm")+
  theme_classic()
```

```{r Construct VCV Matrix for Downstream Analysis}
#construct the vcv matrix:
slopes_species <- caper::comparative.data(
  phy = within_species_linear_models_pruned_tree,
  data = within_species_linear_models_subsetted,
  names.col = species_name,
  vcv = TRUE,
  vcv.dim = 3
)
```

```{r Phylogenetic Meta-Analysis on Slopes}
#convert species_name to factor with levels matching tree tip order
within_species_linear_models_subsetted$species_name <- factor(within_species_linear_models_subsetted$species_name, levels = within_species_linear_models_pruned_tree$tip.label)

#calculate phylogenetic correlation matrix
phy_cor <- ape::vcv(within_species_linear_models_pruned_tree, corr = TRUE)
phy_cor <- phy_cor[within_species_linear_models_subsetted$species_name, 
                   within_species_linear_models_subsetted$species_name]

#run phylogenetic meta-analysis weighted by slope SE, accounting for phylogeny
res <- rma.mv(
  yi = within_species_linear_models_subsetted$slope, #use slopes from each species’ linear model as effect sizes
  V = within_species_linear_models_subsetted$slope_se^2, #weight each slope by the SAMPLING variance of the slope estimate (se^2)
  random = ~ 1 | species_name, #account for species-level variation, allow each species to have its own deviation from overall mean slope
 #this models species-specific effects as random deviations sampled from a shared distribution
  R = list(species_name = phy_cor), #incorporate phylogenetic relationships by including the phylogenetic covariance matrix
  method = "REML", #estimate parameters using restricted maximum likelihood (REML)
  data = within_species_linear_models_subsetted
)
#summarise the model
summary(res)
```

```{r Plot Slope Sampling Variances}

#add significance column based on p-value
within_species_linear_models_subsetted$significant <- ifelse(
  within_species_linear_models_subsetted$p_value < 0.05, "Significant", "Not Significant"
)

#plot sampling variances and scale points according to weights used in model fit (i.e. 1/se^2)
help <- ggplot(within_species_linear_models_subsetted, aes(x = log10(slope_se^2), y = slope, colour = significant, shape=significant))+
  geom_point(aes(size = 1/slope_se^2), alpha=0.50)+ #weighted variance (1/sampling variance) - i.e. the weights used
  xlab(expression(bold("Log"[10]*" of Slope SE"^2*" (Sampling Variance)")))+
  ylab(expression(bold("Slope (" * beta[1] * ")")))+
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype='dotdash', colour='blue', linewidth=1)+
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("Significant" = "red", "Not Significant" = "black"))+
  theme_classic()+
  theme(legend.position='none',
                 axis.text = element_text(size=11),
                 axis.title = element_text(size=11, face='bold'))
help

ggsave("Figures/Analysis of Intraspecific Variation/slopes_versus_slope_sampling_variance.jpeg", help, dpi = 600, width = 10, height = 10, units = "cm")

```

```{r Plot Distribution of Slopes}

#extract fixed effect (i.e. intercept of model) and standard error from REML model
fixed_effect <- coef(res)[1] #note only fit intercept-only model so only one coefficient estimated
se <- res$se #standard error for the slope

#calculate 95% confidence interval manually
lower_ci <- fixed_effect - 1.96 * se
upper_ci <- fixed_effect + 1.96 * se

#plot histogram with both REML and raw mean + CI lines
help_2 <- ggplot(within_species_linear_models_subsetted, aes(x = slope))+
  geom_histogram(aes(y = ..density..), bins = 20, fill = "lightgray", color = "black", alpha = 0.7)+
  ylab("Density")+
  xlab(expression(bold("Slope (" * beta[1] * ")")))+
  #REML mean and CI lines (red)
  geom_vline(xintercept = fixed_effect, colour = "red", linetype = "solid", size = 1)+
  geom_vline(xintercept = lower_ci, colour = "red", linetype = "dashed", size = 0.8)+
  geom_vline(xintercept = upper_ci, colour = "red", linetype = "dashed", size = 0.8)+
  theme_classic()+
  theme(legend.position='none',
                 axis.text = element_text(size=11),
                 axis.title = element_text(size=11, face='bold'))
help_2

ggsave("Figures/Analysis of Intraspecific Variation/slopes_distribution_metaanalysis_ci.jpeg", help_2, dpi = 600, width = 10, height = 10, units = "cm")

```
# Windowing Tree for All Species (n=429)

```{r}

#filter count data to species >10 individuals (i.e. from meta-analysis)
filtered_quant_data <- 
  vertebral_counts %>%
  group_by(species_name) %>%
  filter(species_name %in% all_species$stored_data$species_name) %>%
    summarise(
    total_count = mean(log(total_count), na.rm = TRUE), 
    ln_length_ln_width = mean(ln_length_ln_width, na.rm=TRUE)
  )

#reorder filtered_quant_data to match the tree tip order
filtered_quant_data <- filtered_quant_data[match(all_species$tree$tip.label,
                                                 filtered_quant_data$species_name), ]

#define vectors for downstream analysis
filtered_total_count <- setNames(filtered_quant_data$total_count, filtered_quant_data$species_name)
filtered_body_elongation <- setNames(filtered_quant_data$ln_length_ln_width, filtered_quant_data$species_name)

```

```{r Calculate PICs}

#calculate PICs
filtered_total_count_pics <- ape::pic(filtered_total_count, all_species$tree)
filtered_body_elongation_pics <- ape::pic(filtered_body_elongation, all_species$tree)

#node depths from tips (default)
node_depths <- node.depth.edgelength(all_species$tree)

#total tree height (distance from root to tips)
tree_height <- max(node_depths)

#node age from root
node_ages_from_root <- tree_height - node_depths

# Internal nodes only
n_tips <- length(all_species$tree$tip.label)
internal_node_ages <- node_ages_from_root[(n_tips + 1):length(node_ages_from_root)]

#define window width and split nodes into bins 
age_bins <- quantile(internal_node_ages, probs = seq(0, 1, by = 0.10))  #10 bins
node_bin <- cut(internal_node_ages, breaks = age_bins, include.lowest = TRUE)
table(node_bin)

#assemble into pic dataframe
pic_df <- data.frame(
  age = internal_node_ages,
  age_bin = node_bin,
  tc_pic = filtered_total_count_pics,
  body_elongation_pic = filtered_body_elongation_pics
)

windowed_corr <- pic_df %>%
  group_by(age_bin) %>%
  summarise(
    cor_val = cor(tc_pic, body_elongation_pic, use = "complete.obs"),
    n_nodes = n()
  )

windowed_r2 <- pic_df %>%
  group_by(age_bin) %>%
  summarise(
    n_nodes = n(),
    r2_val = if(n() > 1) summary(lm(body_elongation_pic ~ tc_pic))$r.squared else NA_real_,
    slope = if(n() > 1) coef(lm(body_elongation_pic ~ tc_pic))[2] else NA_real_,
    slope_se = if(n() > 1) summary(lm(body_elongation_pic ~ tc_pic))$coefficients[2,2] else NA_real_
  )

#convert factor bins to numeric midpoints
windowed_r2$age_mid <- sapply(strsplit(as.character(windowed_r2$age_bin), ","), function(x) {
  nums <- as.numeric(gsub("\\(|\\[|\\]|\\)", "", x))  #remove brackets/parentheses
  mean(nums)  #midpoint
})
```

```{r Plot R2 by Node Age Bin}

v1 <- ggplot(windowed_r2, aes(x = age_mid, y = r2_val)) +
  geom_point(colour = "black", size = 3) +
  geom_line(group = 1, color = "black") +
  #scale_x_reverse() +  # oldest nodes on left
  #xlab("Node age (Myr, oldest → youngest)") +
  #ylab(expression(R^2 ~ "of elongation ~ vertebral count")) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = FALSE, colour = "red")+
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ poly(x, 2), se = FALSE, color = "blue")+
  xlab("Node age")+
  ylab("R-squared (variation explained)")+
  theme_classic()
v1
```

```{r Plot Slope by Node Age Bin}

v2 <- ggplot(windowed_r2, aes(x = age_mid, y = slope)) +
  geom_point(colour = "black", size = 3) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = slope - slope_se, ymax = slope + slope_se), width = 0.3) +  # tails
  geom_line(group = 1, color = "black") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = FALSE, colour = "red")+
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ poly(x, 2), se = FALSE, color = "blue")+
  xlab("Node age")+
  ylab(expression("Slope (" * beta[1] * ")"))+
  theme_classic()
v2
```

```{r Sliding Window Binning}

window_size <- 30   #number of nodes per window
step_size <- 2      #how much to slide the window each iteration

#sort by node age
pic_df <- pic_df %>%
  filter(!is.na(age)) %>%  # remove rows with missing node age
  mutate(age = as.numeric(age)) %>%
  arrange(age)

#initialize empty storage for loop
results <- data.frame(
  window_mid = numeric(0),
  slope = numeric(0),
  slope_se = numeric(0),
  r2_val = numeric(0),
  r2_lower = numeric(0),
  r2_upper = numeric(0),
  n_nodes = integer(0)
)

#sliding window loop
for (start in seq(1, nrow(pic_df) - window_size + 1, by = step_size)) {
  window_data <- pic_df[start:(start + window_size - 1), ]
  
  #fit linear model
  model <- lm(body_elongation_pic ~ tc_pic, data = window_data)
  model_summary <- summary(model)
  
  slope_val <- coef(model)[2]
  slope_se <- model_summary$coefficients[2,2]
  r2_val <- model_summary$r.squared
  
  #bootstrap R²
  set.seed(1931)
  boot_r2 <- replicate(1000, {
    sample_data <- window_data[sample(nrow(window_data), replace = TRUE), ]
    summary(lm(body_elongation_pic ~ tc_pic, data = sample_data))$r.squared
  })
  ci <- quantile(boot_r2, probs = c(0.025, 0.975))
  
  # store results
  results <- rbind(results, data.frame(
    window_mid = mean(window_data$age),
    slope = slope_val,
    slope_se = slope_se,
    r2_val = r2_val,
    r2_lower = ci[1],
    r2_upper = ci[2],
    n_nodes = nrow(window_data)
  ))
}

#compare extant slope from PGLS model (1.51067) to slopes for each window and calculate 2-tailed p-value
results$p_value <- 2 * (1 - pnorm(abs((results$slope - 1.51067)/results$slope_se)))

#how many windows is the slope significantly different from 1.511?
table(results$p_value < 0.05) #FALSE  TRUE 326    83 - most windows the slope is not sig. diff. from global estimate from extant species, unlikely to have changed across subfamily diversification (I think)

#what are the global trends?

#fit x^2 linear model for slope and window
lm_slope_poly <- lm(slope ~ poly(window_mid,2), data = results)
summary(lm_slope_poly) #poly fits better, although this is probably not meaningful. 

#fit x^2 linear model for r^2 and window
lm_r2_poly <- lm(r2_val ~ poly(window_mid,2), data = results)
summary(lm_r2_poly) #poly fits better
```

```{r Phylogenetic linear mixed model (slope and residual variance heterogeneity)}

#data is stored here
#all_species$matrix_data

x <- all_species$matrix_data[,3]
y <- all_species$matrix_data[,5]
species_names <- rownames(all_species$matrix_data)

#combine into dataframe (pglmm expects a dataframe)
total_count_body_aspect_ratio <- data.frame(
  species = species_names,
  x = x,
  y = y
)
#remove rownames
rownames(total_count_body_aspect_ratio) <- NULL
#factorise the species name (for some reason)
total_count_body_aspect_ratio$species <- as.factor(total_count_body_aspect_ratio$species)

total_count_body_aspect_ratio
#phylogenetic covariance matrix
A <- ape::vcv.phylo(all_species$tree)

A

total_count_body_aspect_ratio$species == rownames(A)

#fit random-slope PGLMM
plmm_tc_bar <- pglmm(
  formula = y ~ x + (x | species__),  # random intercept + slope with phylogenetic covariance
  data = total_count_body_aspect_ratio,
  family = "gaussian",
  cov_ranef = list(species = A)
)

summary(plmm_tc_bar)

#residuals from the PGLMM
resid_vals <- residuals(plmm_tc_bar)


#combine with species names
resid_df <- data.frame(
  species = total_count_body_aspect_ratio$species,
  residual = resid_vals
)

#absolute residuals
resid_df$abs_residual <- abs(resid_df$residual)

#10 species deviating most
top_deviations <- resid_df[order(-resid_df$abs_residual), ][1:10, ]
top_deviations
```

# Windowing Tree for Species with >10 Individuals (n=176)

```{r}

  vertebral_counts %>%
  group_by(species_name) %>%
  filter(species_name %in% within_species_linear_models_subsetted$species_name) %>%
    summarise(
```

```{r Sliding Window Binning}

window_size <- 20   #number of nodes per window
step_size <- 1      #how much to slide the window each iteration

#sort by node age
pic_df <- pic_df %>%
  filter(!is.na(age)) %>%  # remove rows with missing node age
  mutate(age = as.numeric(age)) %>%
  arrange(age)

#initialize empty storage for loop
results <- data.frame(
  window_mid = numeric(0),
  slope = numeric(0),
  slope_se = numeric(0),
  r2_val = numeric(0),
  r2_lower = numeric(0),
  r2_upper = numeric(0),
  n_nodes = integer(0)
)

#sliding window loop
for (start in seq(1, nrow(pic_df) - window_size + 1, by = step_size)) {
  window_data <- pic_df[start:(start + window_size - 1), ]
  
  #fit linear model
  model <- lm(body_elongation_pic ~ tc_pic, data = window_data)
  model_summary <- summary(model)
  
  slope_val <- coef(model)[2]
  slope_se <- model_summary$coefficients[2,2]
  r2_val <- model_summary$r.squared
  
  #bootstrap R²
  set.seed(1931)
  boot_r2 <- replicate(100, {
    sample_data <- window_data[sample(nrow(window_data), replace = TRUE), ]
    summary(lm(body_elongation_pic ~ tc_pic, data = sample_data))$r.squared
  })
  ci <- quantile(boot_r2, probs = c(0.025, 0.975))
  
  # store results
  results <- rbind(results, data.frame(
    window_mid = mean(window_data$age),
    slope = slope_val,
    slope_se = slope_se,
    r2_val = r2_val,
    r2_lower = ci[1],
    r2_upper = ci[2],
    n_nodes = nrow(window_data)
  ))
}

#compare extant slope from PGLS model (1.51067) to slopes for each window and calculate 2-tailed p-value
results$p_value <- 2 * (1 - pnorm(abs((results$slope - 1.51067)/results$slope_se)))

#how many windows is the slope significantly different from 1.511?
table(results$p_value < 0.05) #FALSE  TRUE 129    27 - most windows the slope is not sig. diff. from global estimate from extant species, unlikely to have changed across subfamily diversification (I think)

#what are the global trends?

#fit x^2 linear model for slope and window
lm_slope_poly <- lm(slope ~ poly(window_mid,2), data = results)
summary(lm_slope_poly) #poly fits better

#fit x^2 linear model for r^2 and window
lm_r2_poly <- lm(r2_val ~ poly(window_mid,2), data = results)
summary(lm_r2_poly) #poly fits better


```

```{r Plotting of Windowed Slope}
  window_mid = seq(0, max(results$window_mid), length.out = 100),
  slope = 1.51067,  # central value
  ymin = 1.51067 - 1.96*0.12599,  # lower bound
  ymax = 1.51067 + 1.96*0.12599   # upper bound
)
```

```{r Filter to Species with 25 (or more) Individuals}
#filter for species which have 25 or more individual specimens
individual_counts_25_above <-
  vertebral_counts_intraspecific_variation_filtered %>%
  filter(n_count >= 25) #25 gives a nice range of species (n=17), some very elongate or deep bodied

#identify species
species_lots_individuals <- individual_counts_25_above$species_name

#filter vertebral counts data (i.e. individuals) to species present defined above
vertebral_counts_individual_counts_25_above <- 
  vertebral_counts %>%
  filter(species_name %in% species_lots_individuals)

#check that it has worked
all(sort(unique(vertebral_counts_individual_counts_25_above$species_name)) == sort(species_lots_individuals))

#filter NA (i.e. missing aspect ratio)
vertebral_counts_individual_counts_25_above <- 
  vertebral_counts_individual_counts_25_above %>%
  drop_na()

#calculate mean and standard error
vertebral_counts_individual_counts_25_above_summary <- 
  vertebral_counts_individual_counts_25_above %>%
  group_by(species_name, total_count) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_aspect_ratio = mean(ln_length_ln_width, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_aspect_ratio = ifelse(n() > 1, sd(ln_length_ln_width, na.rm = TRUE), 0),  # Set SD to 0 if only 1 entry
    n = sum(!is.na(aspect_ratio)),  # Ensure n counts only valid values
    se_aspect_ratio = ifelse(n > 1, sd_aspect_ratio / sqrt(n), 0)  # Set SE to 0 if SD is 0
  )
vertebral_counts_individual_counts_25_above_summary
```
